facts.text: Lakeport was renamed from Milwaukie City by surveyor David Ward, and the Burtchville post office officially became Lakeport on June 19, 1857.
In June 1962, student activists led by Tom Hayden completed the Port Huron Statement at the former UAW retreat in Lakeport’s southern park unit.
Lakeport State Park divides into two units separated by the village, linked by a pedestrian overpass over M‑25 and offering over a mile of Lake Huron shoreline.
Before European settlement, the Ojibwe people inhabited the Lakeport area for centuries, with archaeological evidence dating back to at least the eighteenth century.
The United States Life‑Saving Service opened Lake View Beach Station in Lakeport in 1898, which later became part of the Coast Guard in 1915.
Lakeport’s July highs average 80°F while January lows average 18°F, showing the lake’s tempering effect on extreme temperatures.
